title: Doubling a register into scratch space
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, $b$ a Boolean value, and $st$ a machine state whose seven register values are all at most $B$. If $st.T+2st.S\le B$, then the machine reaches label $\mathrm{mv}(b,0)$ from label $\mathrm{dm}(b,0)$ with state obtained by setting $S$ to zero and replacing $T$ by its initial value plus twice the initial value of $S$, leaving the other state coordinates unchanged. Every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the machine's validity conditions and has all register values at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
For any input bit string $x$, bound $B$, Boolean parameter $b$, and register state
$\mathrm{st}$ whose seven register values are all at most $B$, if $T+2S\le B$, the
machine can reach the state with instruction $\mathrm{mv}(b,0)$ and registers $S=0$ and
$T=T_{\mathrm{old}}+2S_{\mathrm{old}}$, leaving the other registers unchanged. Every
configuration before the final step satisfies the machine's preconditions and has every
register at most $B$.
